title: Theo on founder mode: stay close to users, hire for what you love, ignore investor advice
summary: Theo reacts to Paul Graham's "founder mode" essay with lessons from Ping, UploadThing and Twitch. He argues founders should stay hands-on with support and sales, hire only for work they already love, and not take operating advice from investors or manager-style org structures.

principles.text: Don't hire to escape work you dislike; hire for work you love so you must handle the rest yourself.
principles.quote: stop hiring for the things you don't want to do hire for the things you love to do so you're forced to deal with the things you don't want to do

principles.text: Founders should personally do sales and support at ground level, not delegate it early.
principles.quote: I still take all of the sales calls for all of the services we've built it's important to be on that ground level doing support and being involved in these ways

principles.text: Fast, visible bug fixes build more loyalty than never having bugs.
principles.quote: the most loyal users were the ones who had a bug reported it and then we fixed it really fast and told them when it was fixed and thanked them

principles.text: Hiring too early slows a startup; Theo cut the team back to a tiny core to move faster.
principles.quote: Not only was it just more than we needed it was actually slowing us down

principles.text: Don't take operating advice from investors; they rarely give their real reason for passing.
principles.quote: investors will never tell you the real reason they're not investing

principles.text: Impact, not org chart position, should decide who gets access to leadership.
principles.quote: your org chart cannot and should not represent the amount of impact people are having
